questions_for_advisor: The command's own question — is the freeze absolute, or does the owner want T1 run once? — is the owner's and I have not acted on it. For the ruling: T1 is the only sweep that would produce information the four generations do not already contain, and it is also the cheapest thing to get wrong, because a peak-hour failure is indistinguishable from an off-peak one without a paired control. My recommendation is that T1 waits, not because it is low value but because it needs a paired off-peak arm in the same session to mean anything, and that doubles its cost.

The freeze's third exit condition — one B14 demonstration reaching a terminal — is not yet met. ARCH-20260922-010 ran and its trace was destroyed by executor error before it could be read (see that response). The stdout proves the run did NOT converge: 0/2, with coverage still failing 3 of 5 measurable criteria. So the freeze stands, and whether a re-run is bought is the owner's.
